summary: This note is a short encyclopedia-style entry on Wednesday Addams, the fictional character from Charles Addams' cartoons. It explains that the cartoon family members were originally unnamed and that the name Wednesday was given when the characters were adapted for the 1964 television series, drawn from a nursery rhyme. It also lists her family relationships: sister of Pugsley Addams (and Pubert Addams in the film Addams Family Values), and only daughter of Gomez and Morticia Addams.
one_line: Wednesday Addams is the fictional daughter of Gomez and Morticia Addams, named for a nursery rhyme when the Addams characters reached television in 1964.
key_facts: Wednesday Addams appeared in Charles Addams' cartoons, which first appeared in The New Yorker.
In the original cartoons, Wednesday and other Addams family members had no names.
Charles Addams gave the character the name Wednesday when the characters were adapted to the 1964 television series.
The name Wednesday is based on the nursery rhyme line "Wednesday's child is full of woe".
Wednesday Addams is the sister of Pugsley Addams.
In the movie Addams Family Values, Wednesday Addams is also the sister of Pubert Addams.
Wednesday Addams is the only daughter of Gomez Addams and Morticia Addams.
